sections.text: Advent begins on Sunday, November 29. If you want the Christmas story on your lock screen for the four weeks after it, FaithWall handles the setting, and this page handles the choosing. A **Christmas Bible verse wallpaper iPhone** owners can read in one glance needs a short verse and a clear band under the clock. Below are 18 King James verses, grouped by prophecy, birth, joy and peace, and light, each with its word count. For the year-round setup, see the [guide to daily Scripture on the lock screen](/daily-scripture-lock-screen).
How long can a Christmas verse be on a lock screen?

Our rule of thumb is **about 20 words**. The date, clock and widgets fill roughly the top third of an iPhone lock screen, and the flashlight and camera buttons hold the bottom corners. The verse lives in the band between, and every extra word makes the type smaller. The free web wallpaper maker on this site works the same way: it keeps the verse between those two zones and shrinks a long one to fit rather than letting it run under the clock.

So we counted. Every word count on this page comes from the King James text behind this site's Bible tools, counted on November 17, 2026. Luke 2:14 runs 14 words and Luke 2:11 runs 19. Isaiah 9:6 runs 39, which is why the list splits it in two. That's the test for a **Christmas Bible verse wallpaper iPhone** screens can carry: short enough to read before you swipe up. For picks outside the season, here are [20 short verses that read in a glance](/blog/short-bible-verses-for-lock-screen).

sections.label: of U.S. adults are occasional Bible users
sections.description: They read Scripture three or four times a year to monthly, per the American Bible Society's State of the Bible 2026, which surveyed 2,649 U.S. adults with NORC at the University of Chicago. A verse on the lock screen is there on all the days in between.

sections.text: How do you set a Christmas verse as your iPhone wallpaper?

items: Download FaithWall.
Find your verse by reference or search, in any of 24 translations. Every verse on this page is KJV.
Choose the wallpaper setup. Once you pick the verse, the app runs an Apple Shortcut that applies it, and iOS shows Shortcuts for a moment.
When the season ends for you, after Christmas Day or on Epiphany, January 6, pick the verse that comes next. Until you do, the Christmas verse stays.

sections.content: **No-install option:** our [Bible verse wallpaper maker](/bible-verse-wallpaper-maker) takes any verse you type, a style or your own photo, and exports a PNG at 1179 × 2556 pixels for recent standard iPhones or 1290 × 2796 for Pro Max and Plus models. sections.text: Weighing apps before you choose? Here's [how the lock-screen verse apps compare](/best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps).
18 Christmas Bible verses for your lock screen
They're grouped by where they fall in the story. Each line gives the KJV text and its length, so you can see which ones fit before you choose.
Prophecy and promise

items: Isaiah 7:14 — "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." (24 words)
Isaiah 9:6a — "For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given" (13 of 39 words)
Isaiah 9:6b — "and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace." (26 of 39 words)
Matthew 1:23 — "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." (27 words)

sections.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given
The birth

items: Luke 2:11 — "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord." (19 words)
Luke 1:37 — "For with God nothing shall be impossible." (7 words)
Luke 2:19 — "But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart." (12 words)
John 1:14 — "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth." (30 words)
John 3:16 — "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life." (25 words)

sections.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
Joy and peace

items: Luke 2:14 — "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men." (14 words)
2 Corinthians 9:15 — "Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift." (8 words)
Matthew 2:10 — "When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy." (11 words)
Luke 2:10 — "And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people." (24 words)
Romans 15:13 — "Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost." (27 words)

sections.text: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
Light

items: John 1:5 — "And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not." (12 words)
John 1:9 — "That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world." (14 words)
Isaiah 60:1 — "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee." (17 words)
Isaiah 9:2 — "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined." (28 words)

sections.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

sections.content: **Split long verses honestly.** Isaiah 9:6 is split at its first colon, so the two halves carry an "a" and a "b". Keep that letter on your reference, and read the whole verse once. Micah 5:2, the Bethlehem prophecy, runs 40 words, and its first clause alone runs 30, so it isn't on the list. Read it whole in Micah 5 instead.

sections.text: Where this gets hard: a screenshot isn't a wallpaper

The quick route is a screenshot of a verse from a Bible app, set as your wallpaper. On the lock screen it falls apart: the clock lands on the first line, the app's margins and buttons come along, and the crop cuts off the reference. Then the season moves on, and changing the verse means making, cropping and setting a new image by hand.

**FaithWall skips the image work.** If you want a different verse for each Sunday of Advent, you pick it that Sunday and the app applies it, with nothing to crop. If you'd rather design your own images all year, here's how a [free Scripture wallpaper holds up over time](/blog/scripture-wallpaper-for-iphone-free).

Luke 2:19 says Mary kept these things and pondered them in her heart. A verse you meet every time you pick up your phone is a small way to do the same through December. The best **Christmas Bible verse wallpaper iPhone** screens can carry is the one you'll still be reading on Christmas Eve: short, whole or honestly labeled, and chosen on purpose.
